newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Sun Life says 97 started well.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Sun Life says 97 started well.

text.p: British insurance group Sun Life and Provincial Holdings Plc said on Tuesday it had made a good start to the year and would focus on boosting core profitability at its newly-merged group.

"It's been business as usual to date. There is no reason to believe there is any change in the underlying profitability. We are not displeased with the start to the year," chief executive officer Michael Hart said in a telephone interview.
Sun Life and Provincial Holdings Plc, which groups Sun Life Corporation, UAP Provincial and New Ireland Holdings, floated on the stock exchange in July last year.
Sun Life provides life assurance, pensions and investment products to both individuals and businesses in Britain.
Earlier it said its operating companies' pretax profits rose three percent last year to 181.6 million stg on a pro-forma basis, taking into account the new group structure.
Hart said he was encouraged by the group's performance in the hotly-contested life insurance market.
Pretax profits at Sun Life Corporation rose 23.4 percent to 110.3 million stg on a pro-forma basis last year while the value of new business rose 21.7 percent.
"The fact that we were able to maintain or increase the value of new business in a very competitive market place was encouraging. There is a lot of pressure there," he said.
"We think holding the result at UAP Provincial to pretty well in line with last year is a good performance in an insurance downcycle," he added.
Pro-forma profits at UAP Provincial slipped 1.6 percent despite a 3.8 percent rise in net premiums written.
Hart said the group would now concentrate on shareholder value and profitability after a year marked by the mergers, flotation and restructuring.
"We are concentrating on the core businesses...that's the focus for this year and we don't see any gaps at the moment," he said.

Asked about the implications of the proposed merger between Axa SA and Union des Assurances de Paris, Hart said his group was considering its options. AXA holds a majority stake in Sun Life and Provincial Holdings.

"Basically, AXA has Sun Life and Provincial Holdings, Axa Equity and Law, and Axa Insurance in Britain. Obviously, not to examine what opportunities there might be for that wider grouping of businesses would not make sense," he said.

Hart said his group's exposure to Britain's pensions scandal, where many individuals had been wrongly advised by the industry to take out personal pensions instead of staying in occupational schemes, was not a cause for concern.
The industry is now beginning to compensate victims of pensions misselling in the late 1980s and early 1990s.

"As far as Sun Life is concerned, it has a very small exposure. On opt-outs, there are only 1,000 cases and we have made as much progress as we can...it's not an issue for us. We do not believe there is any need to add to any provisions for that," he said.
